reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Same AI, separate source-first pass after freezing. Began with the UCR 2026–2027 regulations and the curriculum, pathway and cluster pages. Rebuilt the degree structure from the regulations and reconciled all three schedules from the active workbook, then compared the official interest scope, course evidence, titles and explanations with the frozen decision and canonical record.
findings: The Education and Examination Regulations establish an English-taught 180 EC degree. Articles 3.5 and 3.6 require ACCPPDE101 before semester three, 45 EC of advanced work, and a passed LAS Portfolio and Reflection. The portfolio is separate from the course-credit total. Article 4.1 gives 7.5 EC per regular course and 15 EC for a Research Seminar. The two advanced options are six regular 300-level courses or four plus a Research Seminar taken in or after semester five. Article 6.3 awards a BSc for 90 EC across the three science clusters combined including at least 22.5 EC of advanced courses in those clusters. A cluster-specific major requires 75 EC in that cluster including 22.5 EC at 300 level. The generic comparator allows both awards and does not prescribe a disciplinary route. The minimum course credit allocation is 7.5 EC development, 45 EC advanced, and 127.5 EC further choice, which can include additional advanced courses.

The official cumulative milestones are 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 and 180 EC. Each example reaches them with four 7.5 EC courses per semester, takes development before semester three and meets the advanced requirement with regular courses. The broad example includes ten advanced courses, the business and data examples eight each. As scheduled the broad example meets the BA and multidisciplinary conditions, the business example meets the BA and business cluster conditions, and the data example meets the BSc and Data Science cluster conditions. The portfolio and degree examination remain student requirements.

The broad plan illustrates the generic degree through all six clusters. Development, rhetoric, programming and sustainability in the first semester are followed by brain and behaviour, quantitative and qualitative methods, data and political and media studies. It applies these skills in governance, cognition, econometrics, historical research and documentary analysis. The business example develops from product design, venture foundations, economics and accounting into the management and analysis of ventures and markets. Its AI business course concerns organisational and policy consequences. Its later courses add customer research, economic policy, finance, negotiation, marketing and econometrics. The data example develops from programming, data analysis, logic and calculus through algorithms, matrix methods, probability and machine learning to robotics, optimisation, reinforcement learning and neural networks. Software, networks and data management support implementation, and ethics, experimental methods and persuasion support responsible design and communication. Description-only courses were assessed as substantive where their descriptions support the role, including strategy and digital transformation, historical research, econometrics, market research, databases and reinforcement learning. The mandatory development course aligns directly across all columns. Advanced and other course choice are allocations of credits with many qualifying courses, so they are shown separately rather than paired with any single UCR course. The remaining four official clusters each support a credible direction. The existing pair of business and data is retained under the three-example ceiling as the next two official clusters in order, with distinct coherent course sequences.
